candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite quantities into compatible fractional forms before subtraction by finding a common denominator, converting to equivalent fractions, and/or rewriting a whole number with a fractional part such as 0/d.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts include the same preparatory alignment concept: finding common denominators, rewriting equivalent fractions, and expressing whole numbers with 0/d to enable subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Convert a mixed number with an improper or otherwise nonstandard fractional part into a standard equivalent mixed number before subtracting.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: Expert A embeds normalization of malformed mixed numbers inside Align fractional forms, while Experts B and C separate it as its own skill. This is a one-to-many alignment from A's broader S01 to B.S02 and C.S02.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Carry out the subtraction once forms are compatible, including subtracting numerators of like fractions and subtracting whole-number and fractional parts of mixed numbers.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S02 and C.S03 match directly. B.S03 is broader because it also includes regrouping, but it clearly contains the same core subtraction operation.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup by borrowing 1 from the whole part and converting it into fractional units when the fractional part of the minuend is too small to subtract directly.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S03 is a direct regrouping skill. B.S03 combines subtraction and regrouping, so it maps here as well as to the core subtraction concept. C.S04 includes borrowing/regrouping together with simplification, so it partially aligns here.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms and express it appropriately as a fraction, mixed number, whole number, or zero.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S04 and B.S04 match directly. C.S04 is broader because it combines regrouping with final simplification and expression, but it clearly includes this same end-of-solution concept.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks share the same overall workflow for fraction and mixed-number subtraction: prepare compatible forms, perform subtraction, regroup when needed, and simplify the result. The main structural differences are that Expert A folds mixed-number normalization into alignment, Expert B folds regrouping into subtraction, and Expert C folds regrouping into final simplification. All skills were aligned into five underlying concepts, with several one-to-many mappings required because some experts used broader composite skills.
